title: Slain man did repairs for officers; Man shot by police ran electronics shop Wounded sergeant in stable condition after surgery
article: A man shot dead after wounding a Toronto police sergeant with a shotgun blast had often been visited in the past by officers who needed repairs on electrical appliances.
Antonio Bellon, who once operated Croma Electronics in a small shop attached to his Dufferin St. home, was the father of a Toronto police sergeant.
Bellon shut the store abruptly after his wife died a couple of years ago and he became depressed.

Members of the provincial Special Investigation Unit hope that medical records will shed light on the 63-year-old man's mental state before the shooting incident Saturday evening in which Sergeant Allan Jenkins was hit in the shoulder and head with shotgun pellets. The SIU probes cases of serious injury or death involving police.
Family members and neighbours have told investigators Bellon had received psychiatric treatment in the past year and had behaved erratically.
No details have been released, but Rose Hung, an SIU spokesperson, issued a statement saying Bellon had died from a single gunshot wound to the chest.
Police Chief Julian Fantino referred to the incident as "a very serious life and death situation" for the officers involved while addressing a range of policing issues on CBC radio yesterday morning.

"A young officer, one of the officers involved in this particular situation, has but seven months on the job," he said. "I spoke with him. It's a traumatic feeling that they go through. It's difficult for them to sit down and compose their thoughts. It's not as easy as some would expect."
The shooting occurred about 6 15 p.m. Saturday, after three officers responded to a disturbance call and got into a confrontation with Bellon in a lane off Dufferin St., just north of Rogers Rd.

Details weren't confirmed by the SIU, but several witnesses have indicated that Jenkins, Constable Scott Ritchie and another officer ducked into the narrow lane when they saw Bellon nearby, waving a shotgun.
A moment later, Bellon entered the lane and fired at Jenkins, who was hit with pellets in the face and upper shoulder.

As Bellon moved closer and levelled his shotgun at Jenkins, now collapsed on the ground, Ritchie pulled his semi-automatic handgun and fired two shots. The SIU would not confirm whether Bellon had been hit more than once.
SIU investigators have spoken to 10 civilian witnesses and designated a subject officer and two witness officers.
Police spokesperson Constable Mike Hayles said Jenkins, who joined the force in October, 1986, was in stable condition after undergoing surgery.
Hayles said the SIU has allowed police to name Jenkins and supply details on his condition, but has not given permission to release details about Ritchie or the other officer.

Police are also not being allowed to release details about Bellon's daughter. Colleagues said Corrine Bellon, who joined the Toronto police in 1986, had worked in the same west-end division where Jenkins was assigned several years ago.

She worked in the sex crimes unit at headquarters before being promoted to sergeant and transferred to a North York station, where she has worked for a couple of years. She was to start new duties in the professional standards branch at Toronto headquarters today.
The Toronto homicide squad is also investigating and will present its findings at an inquest if the SIU doesn't lay charges.
